chained_stage_advance.defect: lib/stage-graph-cell.js treated a whole Bash tool_use's is_error as 'stage-advance refused'. `stage-advance.js --to X && bash run-tests.sh` with a red test is_error the call although the advance was written, so the node was dropped from the walk.
chained_stage_advance.change: each stage-advance invocation's outcome comes from its own JSON stdout in the tool_result, matched in order to the invocations of the command: {allowed:true,...} = written (exit 0); {allowed:false,...} (exit 3) or {bump_to,...} (exit 4) = refused (scripts/stage-advance.js prints nothing on stdout for exits 1/2/5). When the count of such JSON objects differs from the count of invocations (or there is none) the previous rule (the call's is_error) applies and observed.ambiguous is true; each call records stage_calls[].basis json|is_error.

rung_keys.defect: classify's eligible_max is U1 if ANY --terms term has zero hits, so for the L/XL feature briefs the first rung depends on which nouns the agent chooses (a free variable the brief cannot fix). v1 keys (l-feature/xl none|U0, l-u0-known U0) therefore scored noun choice, not routing. In addition l-u0-known's brief named three new CLI flags (--max-attempts, --delay-ms, --delay-cap-ms) plus 'cap'/'exponential': zero-hit, so U0 was unreachable for an agent that used the brief's own words.
rung_keys.choice: consistency check, not pinned keys with deterministic briefs
rung_keys.choice_rationale: A brief cannot make an honest term list deterministic: the agent decides what its key nouns are, and any pinned rung would again measure that choice. What the guidance can be held to is that the routing follows the probe. The rule keeps two non-vacuous failure modes (rung inconsistent with the terms the agent passed; U0 key without a classify at intent), and every other marker (size/bug/urgent/walk/work) is unchanged. Honest limit: it accepts a U1 that the agent earned, while the walk marker still pins the noresearch walk, so an agent that follows a U1 into the research node still fails on walk. Whether that coupling is wanted is guidance policy and is left to the owner.
rung_keys.rule: the first classify's eligible_max must equal what probe-unknown yields for the --terms the agent passed on the FROZEN BASE tree (a zero-hit term -> U1, --fast-moving -> U2, all hit or no terms -> U0); a classify later than intent may also report U0 for base-zero-hit terms (the agent's own files can create hits). Key U0: classify must be called, and at intent (before any accepted stage-advance to a node other than intent). Key none: no classify passes; a classify must be consistent. Terms that cannot be read statically (shell expansion) or no repo context: the previous pinned rule applies and observed.rung_check.mode is pinned-fallback.
rung_keys.known_approximation: the derivation greps tracked files only; probe-unknown.js also reads .claude/knowledge and the memory dir, which do not exist in a cell
rung_keys.brief_change: tasks/stage-graph-l-u0-known/task.md rewritten so the feature is described only with things that exist in the cell repo (scheduler, retry policy, queue, attempts, delay, backoff, runner, design doc); size, bug, urgent, research, units and the expected walk are identical, answer.json is untouched. The real probe returns U0 for the brief's nouns on the fixture repo.
